label: There is no infinite descending chain of PER_SE_5 actual causes of being
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise, attribution deferred: the relation 'c is an actual cause of the esse of x (ActualEsseCause, mode unspecified, tenseless) and causes it per se, as caused (the primitive per se link AsCaused)' is well-founded, for the supplied per se link. It is an analyst analogue, for causes of esse of unspecified mode, of the per se regress that ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7 declares impossible for efficient causes ('in causis efficientibus impossibile est procedere in infinitum per se'), while that passage allows an infinite per accidens series; ad 7 is not attributed this statement. It is weaker than the unrestricted regress premise fd12ad3d, which implies it for every per se link (strength order); PerAccidensRegressControl satisfies it while fd12ad3d fails. Its content depends on the intended meaning of the primitive AsCaused: with AsCaused everywhere true it coincides with fd12ad3d, and with AsCaused everywhere false it is trivial.
